hero.title: Would You Rather? The couple quiz that will surprise you
hero.description: 30 questions to make impossible choices together. The Would You Rather couple edition: funny, deep, and always surprising.

intro.p1: The Would You Rather game for couples is one of those rare formats that works every single time. No equipment, no complicated rules, just two people, impossible choices and answers that reveal more than you'd think. This quiz offers 30 carefully selected questions to make you laugh, think, and above all, surprise each other.
intro.p2: Whether you've been together for three months or fifteen years, your partner's answers always have the potential to catch you off guard. That's the whole point of the game: it's not a test with right answers, it's a conversation disguised as a quiz.

section1.title: How to play "Would You Rather" as a couple?
section1.p1: The concept is simple, and that's exactly what makes it work. Each person asks the other a question with two options, and the other chooses. No right answer. No wrong one either. Just a choice, and what that choice says about you.
section1.p2: What makes the game interesting as a couple is that you already know each other. You think you know what the other will answer. Then a question comes along, and the answer you expected doesn't come out. That's when it becomes a conversation.
section1.p3: A few unofficial rules that make the game better: ban the "it depends" (it's the answer that kills everything, force the choice even if it's uncomfortable), ask why after each answer (the choice alone doesn't say much, the explanation behind it does), take turns asking questions, and set aside time, a game that starts well can easily last two hours.

section2.title: What you actually learn about each other by playing
section2.p1: On paper, it's a game. In practice, it's one of those rare moments where you ask questions you wouldn't ask in a normal conversation, and the other person answers without having time to overthink what they should say.
section2.p2: That's where the "Would You Rather" game for couples reveals things. Not big dramatic revelations, but small discoveries: a priority you didn't suspect, a fear that surfaces through an innocent choice, a value that comes first when you thought it would be the other one.
section2.p3: Couples who regularly play this kind of quiz often have a better understanding of the little details about each other, not the big life topics, but the subtle preferences, the everyday trade-offs, the things that matter without ever having been put into words. It's actually a great complement for getting to know your partner better on a daily basis.

section3.title: "Would You Rather" variations depending on the mood
section3.p1: The basic format is great for getting started, but there are variations that completely change the feel of the game.
section3.sub1P1: Instead of answering for yourself, each person answers as they think the other would answer. Then you compare. The gaps between what you imagined and what actually comes out are often revealing, and often hilarious.
section3.sub2P1: 5 seconds to answer, no more. It removes strategic thinking and forces instinctive responses. This is the one that surprises the most.
section3.sub3P1: For playing with multiple couples. Everyone bets on the others' answers. Couples who've known each other for a long time often think they'll guess everything, and they get it wrong more often than they believe. If you enjoy group games between couples, this variation is made for you.

section4.title: Questions that really make you think (and those that just make you laugh)
section4.p1: There are two categories of questions in a good "Would You Rather" for couples, and both are useful, but not in the same way.
section4.p2: Light-hearted questions serve to put you at ease, to laugh, to set a rhythm. They don't teach anything deep but create the context for the following questions to land better.
section4.p3: Questions that dig deeper open something up. They touch on real expectations in the relationship, needs that haven't always been clearly expressed. The right ratio in a game is roughly 60/40: enough lightness to keep it a game, enough depth to make it worth having played.

section5.title: Why this quiz works so well for couples
section5.p1: The best questions are those where both options truly have a cost, and where the choice says something real. This format works because it bypasses the usual defences: you're not talking directly about the relationship, but each answer reveals a little more about how you see the couple, daily life, the future.
section5.p2: It's also a format that doesn't put anyone in a position of failure. There's no wrong answer, no score to reach. Just two people discovering, question after question, that they might not know each other as well as they thought, and that's exactly what makes the game precious. If you're looking for other fun activities to do as a couple, you'll find other formats just as entertaining.

faq.q1: How many questions does this Would You Rather couple quiz contain?
faq.a1: This quiz features 30 "Would You Rather" questions specially designed for couples. Each question offers two options with a choice to make. The questions mix humour, reflection and couple topics for a complete and varied game.
faq.q2: Is the Would You Rather game suitable for all couples?
faq.a2: Yes, the "Would You Rather" format works regardless of the couple's age or how long they've been together. The questions are designed to make you laugh and think without ever making anyone uncomfortable. It's an accessible game that requires no preparation.
faq.q3: Are there any spicy questions in this quiz?
faq.a3: This quiz stays in a fun and reflective register, without explicitly spicy questions. The topics covered touch on values, priorities and everyday choices in the relationship. If you're looking for a more intimate version, spicier variations also exist.
faq.q4: Can you play this quiz long-distance?
faq.a4: Absolutely! The "Would You Rather" format is perfectly suited to playing remotely via video call or even by text. Each person can read the question on their screen and give their answer. It's actually an ideal activity for long-distance couples.
